quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Which of these checks should you NOT do before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Test both brakes to make sure the brake light turns on.
Check that the paint has no scratches.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint has no scratches.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition. Check oil and fluid levels. Make sure your headlight, taillight, turn signals, and brake light all work.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should be ready for:

options.text: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out into traffic.
questions.explanation: A parked car may suddenly pull into traffic without warning. Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space if a car pulls out.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down later than normal.
Squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Your bike will speed up slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, keep more distance from other cars, and wait for larger gaps to cross or merge into traffic.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem when the road is wet.
Makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface that makes it hard to control a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal covers. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Motorcycle crashes happen most often to:

options.text: People who know their motorcycle well.
People who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: New riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new, untrained riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it harder to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves help you grip the handlebars better. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in cities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safer when you wear reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When downshifting, go down one gear at a time. Slowly release the clutch between each downshift.

questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need to use a turn signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when you turn or change lanes. Other drivers may not see your intentions. There could be vehicles nearby that you don't see yet.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Should only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good protective clothing should cover your arms and legs completely. It should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or modern synthetic materials give the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Which surface gives the best grip for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are hazardous for motorcycles. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates all reduce grip. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not an adequate replacement for either.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so vehicles in your blind spot can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. You will be able to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope you wake up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.
